fixes.explanation: That's it. "Jesus rebuked the demon. 'Be silent!' He said. 'Come out of him!'" (Luke 4:35). Jesus doesn't argue and doesn't debate. He gives two short commands, and the demon comes out.
Not this time, friend. The words came out of a man with an unclean spirit, and Jesus didn't answer with praise. The text says, "…Jesus rebuked the demon." (Luke 4:35). He spoke straight to the demon.

Right. The demon throws the man down before them all, and it "…came out without harming him." (Luke 4:35). It looks scary, but the man isn't hurt. He's thrown down in front of everyone and still left unharmed, friend.

Good thought, friend, because Jesus does rebuke the wind and the raging waters in Luke 8:24. But not here. In this scene the people say He commands "…the unclean spirits, and they come out!" (Luke 4:36). Keep that other story in your back pocket.
The text doesn't mention a doctor, friend. It says, "…they appealed to Jesus on her behalf…" (Luke 4:38). Her fever was high, and they went to Jesus about it. That's the help the passage names.
That's right. "…laying His hands on each one, He healed them." (Luke 4:40). Each one, friend. At sunset, all who were ill with various diseases were brought to Him.
No, friend. Pharisee isn't the word Luke uses here. The text says, "…because they knew He was the Christ." (Luke 4:41). The demons were shouting, "You are the Son of God!"
Not this one, friend. Baptist isn't the word Luke uses here. Luke says "…they knew He was the Christ." (Luke 4:41). Jesus rebuked the demons and would not allow them to speak.
Yes! The crowds "…came to Him and tried to keep Him from leaving." (Luke 4:42). Jesus had gone out to a solitary place at daybreak. The crowds were looking for Him, and they found Him there.
Not quite, friend. The text says the crowds "…tried to keep Him from leaving." (Luke 4:42). So the word that fits the blank is leaving. They came to Him in the solitary place at daybreak.

No, friend. Luke says the crowds were looking for Him and tried to keep Him from leaving (Luke 4:42). Then Jesus gives His own reason: "…that is why I was sent." (Luke 4:43). Capernaum turning Him away isn't the reason He gives.

The text doesn't give that reason, friend. Jesus says, "I must preach the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns as well, because that is why I was sent." (Luke 4:43). His reason is why He was sent. This passage doesn't mention His family at all.
